cards.explanation: The answer is playing favorites. The wise say, "To show partiality in judgment is not good." A judge who leans toward his buddy is like a cookie scale with a thumb on one side. Everybody who walks in deserves the same fair measure, friends.

The answer is False. The one who tells the guilty "You are innocent…" gets cursed by peoples and denounced by nations. That's a LOT of people lined up against one fella, friends. I'd rather give an honest answer and keep my friends.

The answer is blessing. The text says it will go well with those who convict the guilty, and "…rich blessing will come upon them." Notice that it's the opposite of what happens to the one who calls the guilty innocent. Telling the truth when it's hard has a payoff, friends.
The answer is a kiss on the lips. "An honest answer given is like a kiss on the lips." That's a warm, close picture, friends. An honest word treats you like someone worth being straight with.

The answer is False. The wise say, "Complete your outdoor work and prepare your field; after that, you may build your house." The field comes first and the house comes after, friends. Get the outdoor work done, and then go build.

The answer is testimony without cause. The saying says, "Do not testify against your neighbor without cause…" The trouble is speaking against him when there's no reason for it, friends. A witness is supposed to tell what's true, not just what's handy.

The answer is True. The same verse says, "Do not testify against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive with your lips." Both warnings sit right together, friends. Your mouth is supposed to be honest, whether it's in court or around the neighbor's fence.

The answer is False. The text says, "Do not say, “I will do to him as he has done to me; I will repay the man according to his work.”" Getting even is exactly what the wise tell us not to say, friends. It's hard to hear, I know.
The answer is False. The text says, "Thorns had grown up everywhere, thistles had covered the ground…" Everywhere, friends, not just one corner. That's a field nobody's been looking after.
The answer is broken down. The text says, "…the stone wall was broken down." Thorns inside and a wall that fell apart outside, friends. Nobody's been taking care of that place.

The answer is instruction. The writer says, "I observed and took it to heart; I looked and received instruction…" He didn't just walk past, friends. He looked at that field and learned something from it.

The answer is True. The writer says, "A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest…" Little, little, little, friends. And then the next verse says "…poverty will come upon you like a robber…"

The answer is poverty like a robber. The writer says, "…poverty will come upon you like a robber, and need like a bandit." A robber doesn't knock first, friends. It can feel like it came out of nowhere, but it's those little rests piling up.
